correctness.rationale: For t≠0,1 and p=17 the branch polynomial has six simple roots, defining a smooth genus-two curve. The two explicit quotient maps pull back a basis of holomorphic differentials and induce an isogeny to two elliptic curves. The even sextic forces the Cartier–Manin matrix diagonal; exact binomial expansion modulo 17 gives c16=t⁴(t+3)(t−5)(t²−t+1) and c32=2(t+6)(t−7)(t²−t+1). Their gcd is precisely t²−t+1, which has discriminant −3=14, nonsquare in F17; the other smooth zeros are t=5,7,11,14. Diagonal iterated Frobenius and the elliptic product determine the displayed geometric p-rank, a-number and Newton slopes for all algebraic t. An exact modular reduction shows both quotient j-invariants equal 8 at the common zeros; count over F17 and F17² follows. For p=3,5,7,11,13 exact coefficient-gcd calculations are 1, proving the first-odd-prime assertion. A standalone standard-library verifier was executed from the actual included code and returned VERIFY_OK; finite enumeration is not used as a proof over the algebraic closure. Limits: coefficients describe the marked locus, not distinct isomorphism classes.

originality.rationale: The exact characteristic-17 collision gcd(c16,c32)=t²−t+1, its two conjugate superspecial marked parameters with both elliptic quotient j-invariants 8, four rank-one parameters, complete Newton strata, and the first-odd-prime bound are not statements supplied by the classical genus-two elliptic subcover normal forms. Shaska–Völklein 2001 and Shaska 2012 supply quotient theory, not these arithmetic factors; Harashita–Yamamoto supplies a general Rosenhain superspecial-locus theorem, and Ando counts a distinct genus-two family. Targeted published-finding corpus and literature searches found no equal or stronger explicit claim, but absence in searches does not certify universal priority. Specialized catalogs remain a residual risk.

value.rationale: The two-dimensional classical bielliptic genus-two locus has natural complementary elliptic quotients. Requiring both factors supersingular is an arithmetically meaningful codimension-two condition; this work locates its first odd-characteristic intersection with a fixed natural pencil, proves that the two quotient j-invariants collide at 8, and completely separates rank-zero, rank-one and ordinary strata with their fields of definition. This is a natural complete classification of exceptional reductions, not an arbitrary chosen coefficient or a routine isolated point count. Its use is to distinguish geometry of reductions of the elliptic-subcover locus; broader consequences are not claimed.
